message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"2c9d3f6ac25c58fdb9066a0b9ac57185b978ad920025701f2b6047b28a454af4","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mn-class-d:lineage:69","source_registry_sha256":"960e2daa314aff60b32f5124e42324d79615ce2a3ea953a336216b4593c0c910","units":[{"unit_id":"sec13-u01","module_id":"sec13-m01","objective_ids":["sec13-u01"],"title":{"text":"Your record and losing privileges","fact_ids":["sec13-F01","sec13-F02","sec13-R01"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Driving is a privilege, and your record decides whether you keep it.","fact_ids":["sec13-F01","sec13-F02"]},{"text":"Knowing the three kinds of withdrawal helps you understand every rule that follows.","fact_ids":["sec13-F03","sec13-R01"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Mia got a speeding ticket while visiting another state and wonders whether it shows up at home.","fact_ids":["sec13-F02"]},"reasoning":{"text":"DVS keeps a record of your driving that includes violations in Minnesota and in other states.","fact_ids":["sec13-F02","sec13-R01"]},"result":{"text":"Mia checks her record through the online DVS service and sees the out-of-state ticket listed.","fact_ids":["sec13-R01","sec13-F02"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a license, once earned, is a right that cannot be taken away.","fact_ids":["sec13-F01"]},"correction":{"text":"Driving in Minnesota is a privilege that you can lose by breaking certain laws or failing to meet certain requirements.","fact_ids":["sec13-F01","sec13-F03"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Suspend, revoke, cancel: three doors out, one notice in the mail.","fact_ids":["sec13-F03"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"DPS has withdrawn a driver's license. How will the driver learn what it takes to get it back?","fact_ids":["sec13-F03"]},"answer":{"text":"DPS mails a notice of withdrawal listing the reinstatement requirements.","fact_ids":["sec13-F03"]},"rationale":{"text":"A license can be suspended, revoked or canceled, and DPS mails a notice listing what is needed to reinstate it.","fact_ids":["sec13-F03"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec13-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Keeping your license","fact_ids":["sec13-F01","sec13-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"A privilege, not a right","fact_ids":["sec13-F01","sec13-F03"]},{"text":"Your driving record","fact_ids":["sec13-F01","sec13-F03"]},{"text":"Three kinds of withdrawal","fact_ids":["sec13-F01","sec13-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Driving in Minnesota is a privilege that you can lose by breaking certain laws or failing to meet certain requirements. This chapter explains how that can happen. This first unit covers what your driving record contains, how you can see it, the three ways a license can be withdrawn, and the notice that DPS mails when it happens. It also notes that commercial license holders face their own set of rules. Later units go through the specific grounds for each kind of withdrawal and how to get your privileges back. To restate the key point: Driving in Minnesota is a privilege that you can lose by breaking certain laws or failing to meet certain requirements.","fact_ids":["sec13-F01","sec13-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":46,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Your driving record","fact_ids":["sec13-F02","sec13-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Kept by DVS","fact_ids":["sec13-F02","sec13-R01"]},{"text":"Includes other states","fact_ids":["sec13-F02","sec13-R01"]},{"text":"Serious or repeated violations","fact_ids":["sec13-F02","sec13-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"DVS keeps a record of your driving that includes violations in Minnesota and in other states. Serious or repeated violations can lead to losing your privilege, or to limits on where, when and what you may drive. So a ticket from a trip out of state does not stay behind when you come home. You can get a copy of your own driving record from the state's online DVS service. Checking it now and then lets you see exactly what is on file and catch any problems before they grow into a withdrawal. Put simply: You can get a copy of your own driving record from the state's online DVS service.","fact_ids":["sec13-F02","sec13-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Three kinds of withdrawal","fact_ids":["sec13-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Suspension","fact_ids":["sec13-F03"]},{"text":"Revocation","fact_ids":["sec13-F03"]},{"text":"Cancellation","fact_ids":["sec13-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"A license can be withdrawn in three ways: suspension, revocation or cancellation. DPS then mails a notice of withdrawal listing the reinstatement requirements. Each type has its own list of grounds and its own path back. Suspension covers many violations and misuses of the license. Revocation covers more serious offenses, such as impaired driving. Cancellation applies when you have no legal right to the license. Whatever the type, the notice in the mail tells you exactly what you must do before you can drive again. Remember this rule: A license can be withdrawn in three ways: suspension, revocation or cancellation, and DPS then mails a notice of withdrawal listing the reinstatement requirements.","fact_ids":["sec13-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":45,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u01-s4","kind":"bridge","title":{"text":"Commercial licenses","fact_ids":["sec13-R09","sec13-F01","sec13-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Separate rules","fact_ids":["sec13-R09","sec13-F01","sec13-F02"]},{"text":"Commercial manual","fact_ids":["sec13-R09","sec13-F01","sec13-F02"]},{"text":"Same idea of privilege","fact_ids":["sec13-R09","sec13-F01","sec13-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Commercial driver's license holders can lose those privileges for certain driving offenses, and the Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual covers those rules. This manual focuses on ordinary driver's licenses. The same idea still applies: driving is a privilege that you can lose by breaking certain laws or failing to meet certain requirements, and DVS keeps a record that includes violations in Minnesota and in other states. If you hold or plan to get a commercial license, study that separate manual for its own withdrawal rules.","fact_ids":["sec13-R09","sec13-F01","sec13-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":34,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u01-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the notice","fact_ids":["sec13-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"License withdrawn","fact_ids":["sec13-F03"]},{"text":"How do you learn the steps?","fact_ids":["sec13-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: DPS has withdrawn a driver's license. So the answer is that DPS mails a notice listing the reinstatement requirements. Keep that notice, because every item on it must be met before your privileges can return. Once more: A license can be withdrawn in three ways: suspension, revocation or cancellation, and DPS then mails a notice of withdrawal listing the reinstatement requirements.","fact_ids":["sec13-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u01-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Record recap","fact_ids":["sec13-F01","sec13-F02","sec13-R01","sec13-F03","sec13-R09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Privilege you can lose","fact_ids":["sec13-F01","sec13-F02","sec13-R01","sec13-F03","sec13-R09"]},{"text":"Record covers every state","fact_ids":["sec13-F01","sec13-F02","sec13-R01","sec13-F03","sec13-R09"]},{"text":"Suspend, revoke, cancel","fact_ids":["sec13-F01","sec13-F02","sec13-R01","sec13-F03","sec13-R09"]}],"narration":{"text":"To finish, driving in Minnesota is a privilege that you can lose by breaking certain laws or failing to meet requirements. DVS keeps a record that includes violations in Minnesota and other states, and serious or repeated violations can cost you your privilege or limit where, when and what you drive. You can get a copy of your record online. A license can be suspended, revoked or canceled, and DPS mails a notice listing the reinstatement requirements. Commercial license rules are in their own manual. To restate the key point: You can get a copy of your own driving record from the state's online DVS service.","fact_ids":["sec13-F01","sec13-F02","sec13-R01","sec13-F03","sec13-R09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec13-u02","module_id":"sec13-m02","objective_ids":["sec13-u02"],"title":{"text":"Suspension for driving conduct","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F06","sec13-F07"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Many suspensions come from how a person drives or handles court duties.","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F11","sec13-R03"]},{"text":"Some grounds, like out-of-state offenses, repeat school bus violations or underage drinking, surprise drivers.","fact_ids":["sec13-F06","sec13-F14","sec13-F08"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Leo, who is nineteen, was found by a court to have driven after drinking a small amount of beer.","fact_ids":["sec13-F14"]},"reasoning":{"text":"A driver under twenty-one whom a court finds drove while or after consuming alcohol can have their license suspended.","fact_ids":["sec13-F14"]},"result":{"text":"Leo's license can be suspended even though he was not impaired, because of his age.","fact_ids":["sec13-F14"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a traffic offense in another state cannot affect a Minnesota license.","fact_ids":["sec13-F06"]},"correction":{"text":"A traffic offense committed in another state can lead to suspension if it would be grounds for suspension in Minnesota.","fact_ids":["sec13-F06","sec13-F04"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Repeat, crash, out of state, unfit, bus twice, skip court, underage drink, steal gas.","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F06","sec13-F07","sec13-F08","sec13-F11","sec13-F14","sec13-F16"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A driver was convicted twice in four years of not stopping for a school bus with flashing red lights. What can happen?","fact_ids":["sec13-F08"]},"answer":{"text":"Their license can be suspended.","fact_ids":["sec13-F08"]},"rationale":{"text":"Failing to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights within five years of an earlier conviction can lead to suspension.","fact_ids":["sec13-F08"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec13-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Suspension grounds","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Driving violations","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F08"]},{"text":"Court and fines","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F08"]},{"text":"Underage drinking and gas theft","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"A suspension temporarily withdraws your license. This unit covers the suspension grounds that come from how you drive and how you handle your legal duties. They include repeated traffic violations or a violation that helped cause a serious crash, offenses in other states, medical unfitness, repeat school bus violations, failing to appear in court or pay a fine, misdemeanor traffic convictions, drinking and driving under twenty-one, and gasoline theft. Each one is a reason DPS can take your license away for a period of time.","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":34,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Violations and crashes","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Repeated violations","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F06"]},{"text":"A violation that caused a crash","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F06"]},{"text":"Out-of-state offenses","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Repeatedly breaking traffic laws, or a conviction for a violation that contributed to a crash causing death, injury or serious property damage, can lead to suspension. A traffic offense committed in another state can lead to suspension if it would be grounds for suspension in Minnesota. So your record follows you across state lines, and a single violation can matter a great deal if it helped cause serious harm. Safe, lawful driving every day is the best way to keep your record clean and your license in your pocket. Put simply: A traffic offense committed in another state can lead to suspension if it would be grounds for suspension in Minnesota.","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Medical fitness","fact_ids":["sec13-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Found legally unfit","fact_ids":["sec13-F07"]},{"text":"Unreported conditions","fact_ids":["sec13-F07"]},{"text":"Report what you must","fact_ids":["sec13-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"A court finding that you are legally unfit to drive, or failing to report a medical condition that would cancel your privileges, can lead to suspension. The rule is about honesty and safety. If you have a condition that would affect your right to drive, you are expected to report it rather than hide it. Failing to report it is itself a ground for suspension. If you are unsure whether a medical condition affects your driving, ask your doctor and contact DVS, rather than guessing and putting yourself and others at risk. Remember this rule: A court finding that you are legally unfit to drive, or failing to report a medical condition that would cancel your privileges, can lead to suspension.","fact_ids":["sec13-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":48,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u02-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"School bus: suspension or revocation","fact_ids":["sec13-F08","sec13-F27"]},"lines":[{"text":"Repeat within five years: suspension","fact_ids":["sec13-F08","sec13-F27"]},{"text":"Gross misdemeanor: revocation","fact_ids":["sec13-F08","sec13-F27"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Failing to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights within five years of an earlier conviction for the same offense can lead to suspension. A gross misdemeanor conviction for failing to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights can lead to revocation, which is more serious. So the school bus offense can bring either outcome, depending on the conviction. In every case, the safe rule is simple: stop for a school bus with flashing red lights.","fact_ids":["sec13-F08","sec13-F27"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u02-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Court, fines and misdemeanors","fact_ids":["sec13-F11","sec13-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Failing to appear","fact_ids":["sec13-F11","sec13-R03"]},{"text":"Failing to pay a fine","fact_ids":["sec13-F11","sec13-R03"]},{"text":"Even one misdemeanor","fact_ids":["sec13-F11","sec13-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Failing to appear in court or to pay a fine for a motor vehicle violation when required, or a misdemeanor conviction under Minnesota traffic law, can lead to suspension. If you get a citation, go to court when required or pay the fine on time. Missing a court date or leaving a fine unpaid can cost you your license on top of the original penalty. To restate the key point: A gross misdemeanor conviction for failing to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights can lead to revocation.","fact_ids":["sec13-F08","sec13-F27"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":46,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u02-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Driving conduct recap","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F06","sec13-F07","sec13-F08","sec13-F11","sec13-R03","sec13-F14","sec13-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"Violations and crashes","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F06","sec13-F07","sec13-F08","sec13-F11","sec13-R03","sec13-F14","sec13-F16"]},{"text":"Medical, bus, court","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F06","sec13-F07","sec13-F08","sec13-F11","sec13-R03","sec13-F14","sec13-F16"]},{"text":"Underage drinking, gas theft","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F06","sec13-F07","sec13-F08","sec13-F11","sec13-R03","sec13-F14","sec13-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"To sum up, suspension can follow repeated violations or a violation that helped cause a serious crash, an out-of-state offense that would be a ground here, a court finding of unfitness or an unreported medical condition, and a repeat school bus violation within five years. It can also follow failing to appear in court or pay a fine, even one traffic misdemeanor, a court finding that a driver under twenty-one drove after drinking alcohol, and a conviction for theft of gasoline. Each one puts your privilege at risk. Put simply: A conviction for theft of gasoline can lead to suspension.","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F06","sec13-F07","sec13-F08","sec13-F11","sec13-R03","sec13-F14","sec13-F16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec13-u03","module_id":"sec13-m03","objective_ids":["sec13-u03"],"title":{"text":"Suspension for license misuse","fact_ids":["sec13-F05","sec13-F09","sec13-R02"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Your license is an identity document, and misusing it can cost you the right to drive.","fact_ids":["sec13-F05","sec13-F09","sec13-F10"]},{"text":"Some suspension grounds involve money owed rather than driving.","fact_ids":["sec13-F12","sec13-F15"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Ava's older friend asks to borrow her license to buy beer for a group of nineteen-year-olds.","fact_ids":["sec13-F13","sec13-F05"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Using or lending a license, permit or ID card to buy alcohol for someone under twenty-one can lead to suspension.","fact_ids":["sec13-F13"]},"result":{"text":"Ava says no, because lending her license is illegal and could cost her the license.","fact_ids":["sec13-F05","sec13-F13"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking only the person who takes the license exam for someone else is at fault.","fact_ids":["sec13-R02"]},"correction":{"text":"Allowing someone else to take any part of the license exam for you is a suspension ground, just like taking it for someone else.","fact_ids":["sec13-R02","sec13-F09"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Never lend it, never fake it, never stand in, never lie to police.","fact_ids":["sec13-F05","sec13-F09","sec13-F10"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A driver pays a license agent fee with a check that bounces. When is the resulting suspension lifted?","fact_ids":["sec13-F15"]},"answer":{"text":"Once the check and related fees are fully paid.","fact_ids":["sec13-F15"]},"rationale":{"text":"A bad check brings a suspension that ends once the check and fees are fully paid.","fact_ids":["sec13-F15"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec13-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Misusing a license","fact_ids":["sec13-F05","sec13-F12"]},"lines":[{"text":"Lending and fakes","fact_ids":["sec13-F05","sec13-F12"]},{"text":"Exam fraud and false identity","fact_ids":["sec13-F05","sec13-F12"]},{"text":"Money owed","fact_ids":["sec13-F05","sec13-F12"]}],"narration":{"text":"Your license is more than permission to drive. It is also an identity document, and misusing it can lead to suspension. This unit covers lending your license, fake or altered licenses, fraudulent applications, cheating on the license exam, giving police a false identity, and using a license to buy tobacco or alcohol for minors. It also covers two suspension grounds that involve money: unpaid child support and paying a fee with a bad check. Each one shows that the license comes with duties beyond the road. Remember this rule: Failing to pay court-ordered child support can lead to a license suspension.","fact_ids":["sec13-F05","sec13-F12"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Lending your license","fact_ids":["sec13-F05","sec13-F13"]},"lines":[{"text":"Illegal to let others use it","fact_ids":["sec13-F05","sec13-F13"]},{"text":"Illegal acts bring suspension","fact_ids":["sec13-F05","sec13-F13"]},{"text":"Buying for minors","fact_ids":["sec13-F05","sec13-F13"]}],"narration":{"text":"Letting anyone else use your license or permit is illegal, and using or lending a license for an illegal act can bring a suspension. Using or lending a license, permit or ID card to buy tobacco for someone under eighteen or alcohol for someone under twenty-one can lead to suspension. So even a favor for a friend can cost you your license. Your license identifies you, and only you. Keep it to yourself, and never use it to help someone underage buy tobacco or alcohol. Once more: Letting anyone else use your license or permit is illegal, and using or lending a license for an illegal act can bring a suspension.","fact_ids":["sec13-F05","sec13-F13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Fakes and exam fraud","fact_ids":["sec13-F09","sec13-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Fake or altered licenses","fact_ids":["sec13-F09","sec13-R02"]},{"text":"Fraudulent applications","fact_ids":["sec13-F09","sec13-R02"]},{"text":"Testing for someone","fact_ids":["sec13-F09","sec13-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Having a fake or altered license, applying fraudulently for a license or ID card, or taking any part of the license exam for someone else can lead to suspension. Allowing someone else to take any part of the license exam for you is a suspension ground, just like taking it for someone else. The exam exists to show that each driver knows the rules and can drive safely. Cheating on it puts unprepared drivers on the road, which is why both people involved in a stand-in exam can lose their privileges. To restate the key point: Allowing someone else to take any part of the license exam for you is a suspension ground, just like taking it for someone else.","fact_ids":["sec13-F09","sec13-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":48,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u03-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Both sides of the stand-in","fact_ids":["sec13-R02","sec13-F09","sec13-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Taking it for someone else","fact_ids":["sec13-R02","sec13-F09","sec13-F05"]},{"text":"Letting someone take it for you","fact_ids":["sec13-R02","sec13-F09","sec13-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Many people assume only the stand-in is breaking the rules. In fact, taking any part of the license exam for someone else can lead to suspension, and allowing someone else to take any part of the exam for you is a suspension ground too. Both sides of the arrangement can lose their privileges. The same goes for lending a license: the person who lets someone else use it is breaking the law. If a question asks who can be suspended for exam fraud, the answer includes both people. Put simply: Allowing someone else to take any part of the license exam for you is a suspension ground, just like taking it for someone else.","fact_ids":["sec13-R02","sec13-F09","sec13-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":47,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u03-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"False identity and money","fact_ids":["sec13-F10","sec13-F12","sec13-F15"]},"lines":[{"text":"False identity to police","fact_ids":["sec13-F10","sec13-F12","sec13-F15"]},{"text":"Unpaid child support","fact_ids":["sec13-F10","sec13-F12","sec13-F15"]},{"text":"Bad checks","fact_ids":["sec13-F10","sec13-F12","sec13-F15"]}],"narration":{"text":"Falsely identifying yourself to a police officer can lead to suspension. A bad check suspension, unlike most, has a clear end point: it lasts until the check and fees are paid in full. Remember this rule: Falsely identifying yourself to a police officer can lead to suspension.","fact_ids":["sec13-F10","sec13-F12","sec13-F15"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u03-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the bad check","fact_ids":["sec13-F15","sec13-F12"]},"lines":[{"text":"Fee paid with a bad check","fact_ids":["sec13-F15","sec13-F12"]},{"text":"When does it end?","fact_ids":["sec13-F15","sec13-F12"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a driver pays a license agent fee with a check that bounces. So the answer is once the check and related fees are fully paid. Failing to pay court-ordered child support is another money-related ground for suspension, and both show that unpaid debts can affect your license. Once more: Failing to pay court-ordered child support can lead to a license suspension.","fact_ids":["sec13-F15","sec13-F12"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u03-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"License misuse recap","fact_ids":["sec13-F05","sec13-F09","sec13-R02","sec13-F10","sec13-F13","sec13-F12","sec13-F15"]},"lines":[{"text":"Never lend or fake it","fact_ids":["sec13-F05","sec13-F09","sec13-R02","sec13-F10","sec13-F13","sec13-F12","sec13-F15"]},{"text":"No stand-ins, no false names","fact_ids":["sec13-F05","sec13-F09","sec13-R02","sec13-F10","sec13-F13","sec13-F12","sec13-F15"]},{"text":"Pay what you owe","fact_ids":["sec13-F05","sec13-F09","sec13-R02","sec13-F10","sec13-F13","sec13-F12","sec13-F15"]}],"narration":{"text":"To wrap up, letting anyone else use your license is illegal, and using or lending it to buy tobacco or alcohol for minors can bring suspension.
